text:
[title] Block tables
[body] KV-cache split into fixed-size blocks, mapped per sequence
[body] Copy-on-write shares blocks across parallel samples
[body] Prefix caching hit rate: 61% on the chat workload

novice.takeaway: The slide describes a memory-management technique (block tables) that splits and shares cached data efficiently, boosting reuse rates, to help explain the earlier speedup.
questions: What is KV-cache and why split it?
What does prefix caching hit rate mean exactly?
novice.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe this block-table method improves memory efficiency and speed.

peer.takeaway: The system manages GPU memory for LLM inference by splitting the KV-cache into blocks with copy-on-write sharing, boosting cache reuse via prefix caching.
questions: How does block table structure reduce fragmentation?
What baseline is the 61% hit rate compared to?
How does this connect to the 2.4x speedup claim?
peer.inferred_claim: The presenter wants me to believe block-table memory management is a key technique behind their throughput gains.

expert.takeaway: The slide explains PagedAttention's block table mechanism (fixed-size KV-cache blocks, copy-on-write sharing) and reports a 61% prefix cache hit rate on a chat workload.
questions: How does 61% hit rate translate into latency/throughput gains?
Is block size a tunable parameter affecting this hit rate?
expert.inferred_claim: Block tables with copy-on-write and prefix caching are key mechanisms enabling the memory efficiency behind the claimed speedup.
